overlooked_insights.title: NVDA boardroom coup chatter, Ackman involved
overlooked_insights.insight: Multiple users are discussing a boardroom power struggle at Nvidia, with one linking to an Investing.com article titled 'Ackman blasts Nvidia board over Jensen Huang exit questions fiduciary duties' and another to 'Huang could return as Nvidia CEO -- by friendly means or via a boardroom power play.' Users claim the board ousted Jensen Huang and that a shareholder vote to fire board members is being contemplated. This is a governance story the mainstream headlines only touch obliquely via the TIKR 'CEO Scandals' piece.
overlooked_insights.evidence: Users post links to Ackman-blasting-board and Huang-return articles, plus repeated rants like 'the board wants us dead... time for us to get to firing these board members next vote.'
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Mainstream coverage frames it as a generic CEO-scandal valuation question rather than a live activist/board-fight with named players and a possible proxy vote.

overlooked_insights.title: NVDA $500B chip-financing plan has deployed zero capital
overlooked_insights.insight: Users cite a WSJ report that Nvidia's $500 billion chip-financing plan has deployed zero capital with no deals expected before 2027. This directly undercuts the neocloud business model (CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, APLD) that relied on Nvidia financing to fund chip purchases. No mainstream headline in the dataset mentions this WSJ scoop.
overlooked_insights.evidence: Two separate users paste the same WSJ headline: '$500B NVIDIA CHIP-FINANCING PLAN HAS DEPLOYED ZERO CAPITAL, WITH NO DEALS EXPECTED BEFORE 2027: WSJ' and one explains the ramification for neoclouds.
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: The headline set is dominated by the Anthropic IPO; the financing-plan stall is a slow-burn negative that doesn't fit the 'AI rally' framing.

overlooked_insights.title: Anthropic IPO is circular financing, not cash
overlooked_insights.insight: Users claim Amazon (~14%) and Google (~16%) got their Anthropic stakes not by paying cash but by providing years of free cloud compute, making the IPO a circular deal. One user notes Amazon's stake could be ~25% counting convertible notes; another says Google is adding to its stake rather than trimming at IPO. This ownership mechanics detail is absent from headlines, which just report the $83 price and $81.3B raise.
overlooked_insights.evidence: User: '$GOOGL owns 16% and $AMZN owns 14% roughly!! Neither paid cash to Anthropic, instead they offered years of cloud compute usage for free!! Circular deals.' Another: '$AMZN owns 15% of $ANT, if you count convertible notes closer to 25%.'
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Headlines cover the IPO price and record raise, not the structure of how the strategic holders acquired their stakes.

overlooked_insights.title: Micron buyback window opens Dec 9
overlooked_insights.insight: A user flags that there are '14 trading days until Dec 9 and company can start buying back shares,' implying a buyback blackout lifts then. This is a specific, dated catalyst for MU that no headline mentions (headlines only discuss a possible stock split and earnings revisions).
overlooked_insights.evidence: User message: '$MU 14 trading days until Dec 9 and company can start buying back shares' tagged Bullish.
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Buyback blackout expiry is a mechanical, calendar detail that financial media rarely surfaces unless the company announces a new authorization.

overlooked_insights.title: PANW $4.5B Applied Compute deal scrutiny
overlooked_insights.insight: Users dig into the $4.5B all-stock acquisition of Applied Compute (AI model customization), questioning whether PANW's security customers will actually pay for model-running services, and noting the FY27 revenue guide raise ($395M midpoint) is only about a third explained by the Q1 beat. Headlines report the deal and the 11% pop but not the 'does this cross-sell actually work' debate or the guide-bridge math.

overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Earnings-beat headlines lead with the number; the quality-of-beat and strategic-fit skepticism is left to the message boards.

overlooked_insights.title: CAPR PDUFA Nov 22, label-width is the real swing
overlooked_insights.insight: Users are focused on the Nov 22 PDUFA for deramiocel and specifically on label width: the CEO is reportedly seeking formal approval only for upper limb impairment while trying to get cardiac trial data into the label. Users debate whether the FDA will approve upper-limb only or add cardiomyopathy, and note the FDA often approves early but rejects on the last day. This label-scope nuance is more specific than the 'make-or-break decision' headlines.
overlooked_insights.evidence: User: 'CEO Linda Marbán is not asking the FDA to formally approve deramiocel for cardiomyopathy... instead seeking formal approval only for upper limb impairment while aiming to get the positive cardiac trial data' and 'label width is the swing factor.'
overlooked_insights.why_overlooked: Pre-PDUFA headlines frame it as binary approve/reject; the label-scope question that determines commercial value is a specialist detail.

crowd_vs_news.crowd_view: Users see an active boardroom coup against Jensen Huang, a bogus all-hands that dodged employee questions, and a shareholder campaign to fire the board.
crowd_vs_news.who_is_right: The crowd is closer to the real story: the governance fight is live and named (Ackman, Huang return), which is a bigger overhang than a 1% scandal discount. But the 'board wants us dead' framing is emotionally overwrought; the substance is a genuine proxy fight, not sabotage.

crowd_vs_news.crowd_view: Users are bullish but flag execution details: 30fps isn't constant, some feel 'robbed of $100,' and the real lever is GTA+ subscription conversion plus the eventual PC release.

AMD.summary: AMD is getting a lot of attention online right now, with Reddit mentions jumping from 123 to 191 in the past 24 hours, putting it in the top 3 most-discussed tickers. On Stocktwits, the mood is overwhelmingly bullish—32 bullish tags versus just 3 bearish ones. People are clearly excited about the stock's recent move, especially after AMD jumped 6.6% in a single day while Nvidia lost its after-hours gains. That kind of relative strength has traders talking about a potential short squeeze and a big run in the first quarter. Many are comparing AMD to other chip names like Nvidia and Broadcom, expecting a broad semiconductor rally. There's also chatter about a partnership with BlackBerry (BB) involving QNX technology for robotics, which some see as a long-term growth driver. However, not everyone is convinced. Some point out that AMD's trailing revenue of $45.44 billion is actually lower than Super Micro Computer's $53.99 billion, which raises questions about AMD's valuation relative to peers. Others are puzzled by the stock's sudden outperformance against Nvidia, wondering if it's sustainable. Overall, the community is leaning heavily bullish, but there are underlying concerns about competition, revenue growth, and whether the recent rally is justified. Investors should note that while sentiment is high, the stock's fundamentals are still being debated, and the AI chip race remains fierce. The partnership with BlackBerry is a positive signal, but it's early days. Keep an eye on upcoming earnings and any news on AI chip demand.
